source.title: Beyond Token Positions: Safety Alignment Across Denoising Steps in Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Guoli Wang; Haonan Shi; Tu Ouyang; An Wang

page_placements.theme: Diffusion-language safety depends on positions and trajectories

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how safety behavior responds to early token commitments in diffusion language models, extending shallow-alignment questions to a different generation setting.
record.gate_note: Table 1 directly tests prefilled compliance and refusal prefixes and reports ASR. Figure 3 tests refusal-token commitment at different denoising steps. Table 2 reports refusal-signal and commitment measurements. The paper also reports refusal-token emergence distributions in Figure 1, but those are not KL measurements. RAEC results and ablations are the paper's own decoding method and its performance; they are not counted as tests of whether compliant openings bypass safety. Figure 1 and the intermediate Figure 3 steps are omitted under the row limit.
record.test_reason: Table 1 prefills a compliance prefix into the masked response of safety-tuned diffusion LMs (LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Dream-v0-Instruct-7B) and reports harmful-prompt ASR against the no-prefill baseline. This is a direct V4 prefilling test in a new generation setting (masked diffusion rather than autoregressive). The study is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors name the phenomenon 'shallow-step alignment': early-denoising-step commitments steer dLLM safety regardless of position, and leading positions amplify the effect. Unsafe traces contain refusal signals that fail to persist to commitment. RAEC, a training-free decoding method, lowers ASR while largely preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: Tests prefix prefill and harmful-response ASR in masked diffusion models, where denoising step and response position can be varied separately; no fine-tuning intervention. This is an extension to dLLMs rather than a test of fine-tuning effects.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefill effect varies with response position: effects are strongest at leading positions and decline at later positions. The Figure 3 analysis also reports weaker safety effects when refusal-token commitment occurs at later denoising steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-token top-1 predictions in instruct dLLMs concentrate within the first 8% of denoising steps and the first 2–8% of response positions (Figure 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion LMs, refusal behaviour emerges in early denoising steps and leading positions (a 'shallow-step' analogue of V3, measured by token emergence rather than KL).

fits_no_version.finding: A refusal prefix sharply lowers ASR in base dLLMs, most strongly at leading positions; instruct models stay near their already low baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early committed refusal and compliance prefixes steer dLLM safety in opposite directions, with stronger effects at leading positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Forcing commitment of a single refusal token has its largest effect at early denoising steps and fades after about step 8 (base) or steps 16–32 (instruct).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The denoising step at which a token is committed governs its safety influence in dLLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsafe traces usually contain refusal signals (96–98%) but commit them rarely (2–4.1%) and hold them briefly (4.86–7.41 steps), versus 18.77–21.28 steps in safe traces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-signal persistence and commitment distinguish safe from unsafe dLLM trajectories.

record.problems: The authors state that experiments are largely limited to vanilla dLLM architecture and do not cover safety dynamics during fine-tuning. Reported results provide no uncertainty estimates. Several Figure 3 values are only plotted, not stated numerically.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Figure 1 refusal-token emergence distributions and intermediate Figure 3 intervention steps 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32. Also omitted RAEC's Table 3, evaluator validation, attack results, and ablations because they report performance of the paper's own defense rather than directly testing the claim that compliant openings bypass safety.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning; the Limitations section says fine-tuning dynamics are not covered.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models by position. The Sec. 3.4.1 aligned-minus-base probability shift is only aggregated over an early window, for token selection.

Adversarial suffixes and decoding-parameter changes are not tested as attacks. DIJA is used only as a benchmark variant, without comparison to a no-attack position analysis. Only one compliance prefix string is used, on StrongREJECT.
No deepening training; RAEC is a decoding-time defense.

missing.what: Figure 1 refusal-token emergence distribution by step and position (not KL, but the closest V3-like evidence). It is declared in rows_left_out; noted here for a V3 analogue.
Qualitative examples where the aligned model opens with a refusal, then continues harmful steps after a mid-response compliance prefill, i.e. no recovery past the injected prefix.

record.verdict_notes: V4 holds in diffusion LMs for leading-position compliance prefills. The study reframes the 'opening' as early denoising steps plus leading positions. The reader's V4 links on base-model rows were removed, since base models have no safety to bypass. ASR uses Llama-Guard-3-8B on the full response; no uncertainty is reported. RAEC results (Tables 3–6) are the paper's own defense and were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or measurement of its effect.
No benign-data fine-tuning or measurement of its effect.
The paper measures refusal-token predictions and signals by denoising step and response position, not per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.

Tests compliant and refusal prefix prefilling at response positions in diffusion models. Does not test adversarial suffixes; its RAEC decoding method is a defense, not a test of decoding changes bypassing safety.
No weight or rank localization or editing experiment.
No fine-tuning data or training-objective experiment to explain shallowness.
RAEC is a decoding intervention, not training that deepens safety alignment; no such training or durability experiment is reported.

relationships.condition: Compliance prefill at the leading response position (1%) and at 12.5%, both instruct dLLMs; LLaDA at all positions
relationships.display_finding: A leading compliance prefill raised ASR from 1.29 to 93.93 on LLaDA and from 1.92 to 74.12 on Dream. LLaDA stayed elevated at every position (29.71–93.93), and Dream reached 31.63 at 12.5%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Compliance prefill at the leading response position (1%) and at 12.5%, both instruct dLLMs; LLaDA at all positions
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms substantial ASR increases over baseline for T1-LI-C1, T1-LI-C12, T1-LI-C25, T1-LI-C50, T1-LI-C75, T1-DI-C1 and T1-DI-C12.

relationships.condition: Compliance prefill placed later in the response (25–75%), Dream-v0-Instruct-7B
relationships.reason: The bypass weakens sharply with prefix position: 20.45 at 25%, and only 5.11 vs 1.92 at 50% and 75% (T1-DI-C25, T1-DI-C50, T1-DI-C75). So the effect depends on placement and model.
relationships.display_finding: The bypass weakens sharply with position: ASR is 20.45 with the prefill at 25% of the response, and only 5.11 and 1.92 at 50% and 75%.

relation.reason: Table 1 measures unsafe compliance after prefilling against the initial ASR, providing direct behavioral evidence on V4.

tranche.reason: Section 3.2 directly tests compliance prefilling and harmful-response ASR in masked diffusion language models, extending V4 to a new generation setting.

source_check.notes: Table 1 tests one compliance-prefix string in a 128-token response, with ASR judged by Llama-Guard-3-8B; safety dynamics during fine-tuning are explicitly untested. Table 2 measures refusal-token signals and persistence, not the per-token KL concentration specified by V3.
